A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T2 relaxation times of human articular hyaline cartilage can be measured in vivo with high reproducibility and accuracy using a dedicated multiecho sequence variant at 1. 5 T.

the best results for T2 mapping in human patellar cartilages were obtained with a multisection multigradient echo acquisition technique with optimized section profiles and an improved gradient scheme for stimulated echo suppression.

the best sequence design for T2 quantitation of cartilage in a clinical setting at 1 T is the sequence design using an improved section profile and a spoiler gradient for suppression of stimulated echo effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T2 relaxation times in articular cartilage are not easily determined.
the sequence variant we developed and tested is a robust and valid tool for clinical T2 mapping of articular cartilages at 1. 5 T.
the choice of the sequence variant is crucial and should be based on the specific application and the respective tissue.
